skill.name: segment-cdp
skill.description: Guidance for Segment Customer Data Platform implementations, including Analytics.js, server-side tracking, tracking plans, identity resolution, destinations, and data governance.
skill.summary: Plan and review Segment CDP tracking patterns for browser, server, and governance workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns in this prompt-only skill. Manual review found no executable code, prompt injection attempt, or semantic request for data exfiltration. No remediation is required.

content.value_statement: Segment implementations often lose consistency across browser, server, and destination workflows. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for tracking design and governance.
actual_capabilities: Explains Analytics.js browser tracking patterns for page, track, identify, and group calls.
Guides server-side tracking decisions with @segment/analytics-node concepts and batching behavior.
Supports tracking plan design using object and action event naming.
Highlights identity resolution flow, including anonymous ID behavior before identify calls.
Connects event schemas to Segment Protocols enforcement and validation rules.
Flags common tracking anti-patterns such as dynamic event names and missing identify calls.
limitations: It does not include executable SDK code or installable helpers.
It does not validate a live Segment workspace or real destination configuration.
It does not replace privacy, consent, or legal review for customer data collection.
It provides high-level sharp-edge guidance rather than complete operational runbooks.

use_cases.title: Design a Product Tracking Plan
use_cases.description: Create consistent event names, required properties, and validation rules before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Review Browser and Server Tracking
use_cases.description: Check whether page, track, identify, group, and backend events follow Segment implementation patterns.

use_cases.title: Improve Data Governance
use_cases.description: Identify weak event schemas and connect tracking plans to Protocols enforcement decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Map Basic Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define Segment events for a new signup flow. Include event names, key properties, and where identify should happen.

prompt_templates.title: Review Analytics.js Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned Analytics.js flow. Check page, track, identify, and group usage for ordering issues and missing context.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Server Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Design server-side Segment tracking for backend lifecycle events. Explain which events belong on the server and which data should be minimized.

prompt_templates.title: Govern a Tracking Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Segment tracking plan for Protocols enforcement. Identify naming drift, missing required properties, and risky event design.

output_examples.input: A team needs tracking for account creation, email verification, and first project creation.
output: Recommended event set with object and action names.
Identify timing for the authenticated user transition.

output_examples.input: A backend service sends billing and webhook events to Segment.
output: Sensitive data minimization notes before sending events.

output_examples.input: A data team wants to reduce inconsistent product analytics events.
output: Anti-patterns to remove from future implementation work.

best_practices: Use object and action event names that remain stable across teams.
Call identify before user-scoped track events when the user is known.
Define required properties and validation rules before enabling broad destination forwarding.
anti_patterns: Creating dynamic event names that encode user actions or variable values.
Using tracking properties as separate events instead of structured event attributes.
Sending sensitive customer data without a minimization and governance review.

faq.question: Does this skill write Segment implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and review patterns, not executable SDK code.

faq.question: Can it help with Analytics.js planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers browser tracking concepts for page, track, identify, and group calls.

faq.question: Does it cover server-side tracking?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes when backend events and @segment/analytics-node patterns are useful.

faq.question: Can it replace Segment Protocols?
faq.answer: No. It can help design schemas, but Protocols must enforce them in Segment.

faq.question: Is this suitable for privacy review?
faq.answer: It can support data minimization discussions, but it does not replace legal or privacy review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
